title: Long PLTR — Government AI Monopoly + Iran Geopolitical Premium
entry: Initiate $130–135 (current zone). No macro pre-condition required — government AI is not PCE or Iran-correlated. Scale: 70% at current; add 30% on any pullback to $125–128 or on confirmed SPX BUY upgrade post-PCE resolution. Avoid chasing above $138 without a catalyst.
stop_loss: $122 daily close (~8% below entry midpoint $132.50) — implies a broad growth-stock selloff driven by Fed rate hike signal at June FOMC, OR PLTR's Q2 FY2026 revenue guidance misses significantly
targets: $145 — recapture 52-week mid-range; government contract growth re-rating, +9.4%
$162 — AI Platform commercial ramp + Gotham government expansion; August earnings catalyst setup, +22.3%
$185 — full government AI monopoly re-rating; international defense contracts materialize; August earnings beat, +39.6%
catalyst: US military strikes on Iranian facilities (May 27–28) confirm the Iran war is in active military exchange phase, directly accelerating demand for Palantir's Gotham AI platform, which is deployed by the US Army, Navy, Air Force, NSA, and CIA for real-time targeting and intelligence synthesis. When US forces conduct kinetic operations in a theater as complex as Iran — with thousands of daily intelligence data points, satellite imagery, intercepts, and pattern-of-life analysis — Gotham is the operational AI layer enabling command decisions. Active military exchange is the highest-utilization scenario for Palantir's government contracts. Additionally, Q1 2026 revenue grew 85% YoY to approximately $1.56B, and management raised FY2026 guidance to $7.66B ($637M/quarter run-rate), demonstrating durable fundamental acceleration independent of geopolitical events.
thesis:
Palantir occupies a unique position in the AI landscape: it is the only company whose AI platforms are operationally deployed at scale in active US military and intelligence operations, with multi-year, non-cancellable government contracts that are entirely insulated from consumer cyclicality, Fed policy, and AI spending debates. While NVDA, AMD, and AVGO face quarterly GPU order variability, PLTR's Gotham and Foundry platforms are embedded as mission-critical infrastructure — the software layer that makes sense of the raw compute that NVDA's GPUs provide. When the US strikes Iran, PLTR's utilization rates go up, not down.

The geopolitical premium has three independent channels. First, active Iran operations increase Gotham's intelligence and targeting workload, which is reflected in contract extension and scope-expansion discussions that typically follow major operations cycles. Second, the DoD's AI budget is structurally growing: the FY2026 defense appropriations bill included a 23% increase in AI/autonomous systems spending. RKLB's $816M SDA contract (announced May 27) is the most recent data point confirming government AI spending acceleration. Third, European NATO allies — watching active US-Iran military exchanges — are accelerating their own defense AI procurement under NATO's Palantir Foundry deployment framework, which has been expanding to UK, France, Germany, and Poland since 2024.

The commercial AI Platform (AIP) segment is the underappreciated growth lever. PLTR reported Q1 AIP revenue growing 85% YoY, with US commercial customers growing 71% YoY to 139 customers. The AIP bootcamp model — where Palantir's engineers deploy an AI workflow in a customer's environment in 5 days and then convert that to an annual contract — has an approximately 80% conversion rate and is scaling rapidly into Fortune 500 manufacturing, healthcare, and energy companies. The $7.66B FY2026 guide implies Q2–Q4 acceleration from the Q1 run-rate, suggesting the AIP commercial ramp is in an early-growth phase. August 10 earnings is the next major catalyst.

The entry at $132.51 reflects a -36% drawdown from the 52-week high of $207.52 — driven primarily by multiple compression from the 60x+ revenue valuation that the stock commanded at its peak. Today's -2.59% pullback is a rotation out of high-multiple tech on Iran/PCE uncertainty, not a fundamental deterioration. With revenue growing 85% YoY and government contracts completely non-cyclical, the multiple compression represents an opportunity for re-entry on a stock that has validated its fundamental thesis repeatedly.
bull_case: Iran military exchange broadens and US deploys additional AI-driven intelligence assets; PLTR receives emergency contract expansion from multiple agency clients. Q2 FY2026 revenue beats at $1.7B+ (vs. $1.56B Q1); AIP commercial customers grow to 175+; August earnings triggers analyst upgrades. Stock re-rates from 85x trailing revenue to 95x on growth acceleration. Target 2 ($162) in sight within 6 weeks. Tail: DoD awards PLTR a multi-year national AI infrastructure contract exceeding $2B — resets the government TAM estimate for analysts.
bear_case: Iran military operations de-escalate quickly; government AI spending shifts away from PLTR toward in-house DoD programs; AIP commercial growth decelerates to 40–50% YoY. Multiple compression from Fed June rate hike signal drives PLTR below $122 stop. Structural risk: PLTR's valuation at 85x trailing revenue requires sustained 80%+ growth — if growth normalizes to 40–50%, the stock could trade toward $90–100. The 52-week low of $118.93 represents the floor in this scenario.
invalidation: $122 daily close, OR Q2 FY2026 revenue guidance below $1.5B at August earnings, OR Iran military exchange concludes with a formal ceasefire reducing geopolitical risk premium across defense AI sector

outcome.outcome_label: Target 1 hit — PLTR +9.21% on May 29, closing $156.54
outcome.note: Palantir surged +9.21% on May 29 (from $143.34 to $156.54, range $143.34–$157.78), clearing Target 1 ($145) decisively. The catalyst: IRGC warning shots at four vessels near Hormuz on May 29 and ongoing US military strikes on Iranian facilities confirmed the highest-utilization scenario for Palantir's Gotham AI targeting and intelligence platform. Return from reference price $132.51 to closing price $156.54 = +18.1%; profit-take at Target 1 ($145) represents +9.4% from reference. Stock held $156.38 on May 31, indicating Target 2 ($162) remains in sight for any re-entry on a pullback.
